subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy such as `all | final | off`, or should the supported operator contract remain the existing boolean `messages.suppressToolErrors` plus targeted safety fallbacks?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but the remaining fix changes public config and decides when user-visible failed mutations may be hidden after a success-looking final answer; code inspection cannot safely choose that product/safety contract.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented opt-in policy that keeps current `all` behavior by default, treats the existing boolean as the `off`/internal-only path, and adds `final` only with strict acknowledgement/success tests.

options.title: Constrain to existing boolean
options.body: Do not add `final`; document `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported hosted/team-chat suppression knob and keep safety warnings visible by default.

options.title: Fold into warning router design
options.body: Defer this specific knob and design it together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45565 so tool, lifecycle, and system notices share one category/destination policy.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented opt-in policy that keeps current `all` behavior by default, treats the existing boolean as the `off`/internal-only path, and adds `final` only with strict acknowledgement/success tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged narrow warning-policy fixes and explicitly kept this issue as the broader follow-up.
